exposure: BMI trajectories from birth to young adulthood
outcome: Lipids (total cholesterol, triglyceride, low-density lipoprotein, high-density lipoprotein, LDL/HDL ratio)
cohort: Participants from the Swedish BAMSE birth cohort (n=3204) were followed from birth until 24 years of age.
finding: Participants with persistently high or accelerated increasing BMI trajectories from birth to young adulthood showed elevated levels of cardiometabolic risk markers at young adulthood compared to those with stable normal BMI.
